subject: How to get the same color for populations each run when visualisering minimum spanning tree

messages.author: bed7c1348ff0ff5f
messages.subject: How to get the same color for populations each run when visualisering minimum spanning tree
parts:
Dear Zhian,

When I use the function plot_poppr_msn, how can I get the same color for populations each run? because R choose random colors for each run. Aslo the same function plot_ly when I use it to plot the priciple component analysis (pca). I do not know if there is any function or parameters that can fix the colors for each run, or should I have to call a colors file to define the colors for each population?

Hope to hear from you and thank you.

Best regards
Ying

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] How to get the same color for populations each run when visualisering minimum spanning tree
parts:
Hello,

plot_poppr_msn should not plot random colors for your populations. It defaults to the color palette that was used to generate the minimum spanning network.

One way to specify a palette, however is to use a named vector and use that in the `pal` parameter:

mypalette <- c(Pop1 = "orange", Pop2 = "grey", Pop3 = "powderblue")

Again, I can't give you any information on the plot_ly function since that is not a function that is in poppr.
